newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African gold shares took a battering on Wednesday as the bullion price lost all Tuesday's gains and fell to $351 an ounce, threatening to test the key $350 an ounce level.
Having climbed nearly five percent on Tuesday, riding the brief rally in the gold price, gold shares shed more than three percent.
Dealers said the strong rand -- last bid at 4.5600 against the dollar -- had compounded weakness by eroding any support metal stocks might have won from it.
"Golds looked pretty shoddy actually. Bullion has taken a fall again and the guys are talking about it in the $340s soon. Gold is definitely not the place to be right now," one dealer said.
The gold index lost 43.8 points to 1,385.3 points.
Freegold lost 140 cents to 32.70 rand, Western Areas lost 225 cents to 54 rand, Kloof was off 125 cents to 33.50 and Gold Fields lost 375 cents to 106 rand.
Dealers said that a significant end to losses on the gold board was unlikely to take place in the near future.
Industrial shares also took a bashing, with the index shedding 48.5 points to 6,687.5.
Local shares were punished by volatility on Wall Street, which saw the U.S. stock market gain 100 points before shredding these gains to end weaker.
"The (local) market came down. It was very, very perturbed about Wall Street's strong reversal. This was quite concerning," said Raymond Goss, portfolio manager at Irish & Co.
He said that Wall Street had spooked the South African market and that all eyes would now be on the U.S. markt's open.

"It's (Wall Street) extremely volatile at the moment and everyone is watching it. If there is a Wall Street bounce or it moves up strongly tonight then our market could go very strong tomorrow," Goss said.
Overall trade had been mixed, dealers said.
"It was slow then fast, up, then down," one dealer said.
"It was fast and furious. It depends where you were," Goss said. Volumes for the day had been good.
Weakness in golds and industrials combined to knock the all-share index 48.5 points down to 6,687.5.
Equity futures contracts suffered the same fate as stocks.
Gold contracts stumbled on weaker bullion and failed to break much away from starting levels.
Industrial contracts slipped, spooked by Wall Street's rapid reversal of Tuesday's gains.
Dealers said that futures fulfilled expectations by trying the downside.
The March all-share contract stands at 6,100/30 from 6,189, the industrial contract is at 7,803/13 from 7,887 and the gold contract is at 970/80 from 1,002.
-- Melanie Cheary, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482 1003
